questions.q: A Temporal user asks for Restate's equivalent of an activity. What do you tell them?
questions.why: Both are 'a side effect, executed and recorded'. Restate keeps them inline; Temporal keeps them in separate functions.

questions.q: Your code is down. Which platform reports errors, and which waits silently?
options: Restate reports connection errors; Temporal waits silently on the task queue
Temporal reports errors; Restate waits silently
questions.why: Push (Restate) means the server tries to call you and records the failure. Pull (Temporal) means work waits until a worker asks for it.

questions.q: What's the closest Temporal equivalent of a Restate virtual object?
options: An entity workflow with signals, updates and queries
questions.why: One long-running workflow per entity, changed by messages and read by queries.

questions.q: How does each platform keep in-flight work on compatible code by default?
options: Restate pins invocations to their deployment; Temporal needs patched() or Worker Versioning
questions.why: Restate's deployments are immutable and invocations are pinned. In Temporal any worker may replay any execution unless versioning is configured.

questions.q: A prospect runs everything on serverless functions. Which architectural property makes Restate a natural fit?
options: Push-based invocation plus suspension: functions only run while there's work
questions.why: Restate calls the function when there's work and suspends waiting invocations, so nothing runs (or bills) while waiting.
